 Yaxel Lendeborg makes brutally honest admission after Warriors' 38-point defeat 
 2026-11-14 06:12 
 Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg expressed his frustration following a 123-85 blowout loss to the San Antonio Spurs, admitting that the defeat had taken a mental toll on him.

 The Golden State Warriors suffered a crushing defeat on Friday night, as the San Antonio Spurs dominated them from start to finish in a 123-85 blowout victory.

 Playing without injured superstar Stephen Curry , the Warriors had no answers on either end of the floor, eventually falling to a humiliating 38-point defeat.
 Following the game, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg didn't hold back when discussing his team's disappointing performance in San Antonio.
 Yaxel Lendeborg admits mental frustration after brutal loss
 Lendeborg expressed his frustration with the Warriors' performance, admitting that nothing seemed to go right throughout the game. The rookie was particularly critical of his own struggles, revealing just how much the defeat affected him mentally.
 "We got the shit beat outta us, I don't know what to learn, man. I was flustered the entire game, man. Couldn't make a damn layup .... I just wasn't being aggressive ... I'm not gonna move past this ... I can't throw a damn thing out the window," Lendeborg stated postgame, via Joseph Dycus.
 "We just lost by like 100. So, you know, I'm fu*ked up mentally right now. We got a game in 2 days ... We'll see how we can bounce back," he added.
 Lendeborg struggles as Warriors fall to 8-5
 Lendeborg endured one of his worst performances in a Warriors uniform, finishing with just three points on a dismal 1-of-13 shooting from the field. He also recorded seven rebounds and three turnovers in the loss.
 The performance was especially disappointing considering how impressive the rookie had been leading up to Friday's matchup.
 Before facing the Spurs, Lendeborg had been enjoying an outstanding start to the season, averaging 20.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 3.5 assists in approximately 32 minutes per game.
 With Friday's defeat, the Warriors dropped to 8-5 on the season and sit seventh in the Western Conference standings.
 Golden State will now look to bounce back on Monday when it travels to New Orleans to take on the Pelicans.
